questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I study Japan Studies, and thus never really considered going anywhere else than Japan. I chose Ritsumeikan University primarily because i wanted to study in Kyoto, which is famous for its cultural and historical significance as well as being a place where one can experience a mix of both traditional and contemporary Japanese culture. Furthermore i had earlier heard a lot of positive things about Ritsumeikan University.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy. At the dormitory i lived at, we had assigned mentors who helped us with doing all the procedures upon arrival, as well as making sure that we were comfortable.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: As described above, the mentors at the dormitory helped us fill out paperwork as well as taking us to the local ward office to make sure all was done correctly.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy, as it was done through the application process. I just made a priority list of the available options presented. I was very happy with living at Tokiwa International House. It was not as big as Taishogun Dormitory, and it felt like being a part of a family. The downsides is that the building is pretty old, and as such many of the facilities can feel a bit old.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: In Ritsumeikan i dont believe that any options are provided to live on campus, and i dont think i ever had any problems with it. All the dormitories are quite close to the campus anyway.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: As described earlier i applied through the application process and it was very easy to do.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The administration at Ritsumeikan was very quick at responding to the few problems i had during the application process.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I felt that some of the syllabus descriptions of the RCE (Regular Courses in English) courses were somewhat not corresponding to the actual contents, but in the end i was quite satisfied, though i didnt think that there were enough different options to choose from.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember to apply for scholarships, which is also done through the application process. A lot of my friends from my exchange were very sad that they didnt apply, as it is very easy.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took the IJL (Intensive Japanese Language) track and as such the primary focus was on Japanese language classes. These took up the VAST majority of my time as they are very time-intensive courses, and takes much more work per credit compared to other courses. I was very glad i took the japanese courses as they improved my language skill considerably, but as it is required to take at least 14 credits to correspond to 30 ECTS, i had quite a bit more work than anyone else on the dormitory, and Ritsumeikan themselves doesnt recommend taking courses besides the IJL courses if you take those (IJL takes up 8 ECTS).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
I was very happy with my Japanese courses. As they were conducted entirely in Japanese they took a lot of work, but at the same time forced me and my class-mates into speaking more Japanese which i really liked.
The RCE courses i attended was in general a bit disappointing, compared to UCPH. Though each course had its pros and cons, they were either very easy or not taught in a very engaging way. Though i liked a lot of the contents of all my RCE courses and learned a lot, there were still problems.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
IJL Level 4 
Introduction to Vernacular Culture
Selected Problems in Humanities
South East Asian Area Studies.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: IJL courses. They were by far the most giving to me, even though they were very work-intensive, i still think it was a huge gift to have taken these courses.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There are quite a bit of extra insurance and stuff you have to pay either to the government or to the COOP center at campus.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Shinkansen is very expensive, and sometimes it is worth it to go by plane instead.
General living cost is pretty cheap compared to Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ritsumeikan has a lot of club activities with everything from martial arts to a cat-feeding club. They also host a lot of other events, often organized by the student clubs.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Attend the school festival, and if you want to learn Japanese, there are a lot fo good options to meet Japanese students at the student-clubs.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go on hikes. There is so much beautiful nature close to Kyoto and many hikes of varying difficulty. 
I went to Ise-ken, which was a very good experience, both with beautiful nature and a lot of exciting history.
I would also recommend to just explore Kyoto, the city has so much to offer (especially if you like visiting shrines or temples).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy i would say. Though there are a lot of differences between Denmark and Japan (such a the biking culture or the fact that there are no bins anywhere), i would still say that it was a good experience.  The Japanese people i met were for the most part very friendly, and pretty much everyone you meet will wants to help you if you need anything.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: As described, sign up for student clubs. Furthermore, there is an international community area called Beyond Borders Plaza (BBP) where both Japanese and international students meet up for either language exchange or just to hang out.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I think the most challenging part about Japan is the language. If you dont know any Japanese it can often be a bit difficult to communicate as many people only know a litte, if any, english.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food, the hospitality, the shrines and temples.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Make sure you think about what kind of housing you want. I would definitely recommend to live in a dormitory as it helped me out tremendously both with doing paperwork, as well as meeting new friends from around the world.
Make sure that you choose your courses carefully and choose something that you are sure will get approved by UCPH, as it can otherwise be quite a mess to change courses.
If you dont know any Japanese, study basics on Duolingo or the like, it will improve you experience considerably.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you live in a dorm, make sure to use your mentors and ask them about anything.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I made friends from all over the world, which i am very glad i did. I also improved my Japanese language capabilities so much.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: For me, it was missing home and the family, friends and my girlfriend who i have here. But practically i think it was that i had so many classes compared to many other students that i had to spend a bit more time studying than others.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
